tagline: Cameroon's economic capital on the Wouri estuary, its islands and resort coast reached by pirogue and a single congested bridge.
summary: Douala sits on the southeastern shore of the Wouri River estuary, Cameroon's largest city, main seaport and industrial heart. The estuary is broad and sheltered, dotted with fishing islands such as Manoka, while the wider Bight of Biafra coast holds the black-sand resort town of Limbe beneath Mount Cameroon and, further south, the deep-water port and beaches of Kribi. Cross-estuary and coastal movement is served today by pirogues and by a road network that funnels over the Wouri bridges, leaving the water itself under-used for passenger transport.

demand_signals.label: Wouri estuary crossings
demand_signals.note: The estuary separates Douala's districts and fishing islands; movement leans on pirogues and a congested bridge corridor.

demand_signals.label: Limbe & Kribi coast
demand_signals.note: Black-sand beaches at Limbe and the resort/port beaches of Kribi draw domestic and regional leisure demand along an under-served coast.

demand_signals.label: Port-city congestion
demand_signals.note: Douala's road network is heavily congested around the port and the Wouri crossings, a classic case for a parallel water tier.

demand_signals.label: Regional port hub
demand_signals.note: As the gateway port for Cameroon, Chad and CAR, Douala concentrates business travel that a fast estuary/coastal link can serve.

use_cases.title: Estuary island link
use_cases.body: A scheduled, weatherproof service from the Bonanjo waterfront to Manoka and the estuary fishing islands replaces slow, unscheduled pirogues.

use_cases.title: Resort-coast run
use_cases.body: A coastal link from Douala across the estuary mouth to Limbe's beaches opens a fast leisure route that today means a long congested drive.

use_cases.title: Port-bypass commuter hop
use_cases.body: Intra-estuary hops let commuters bypass the congested Wouri bridge corridor between riverfront districts.

use_cases.title: Southern coastal express
use_cases.body: A longer-range coastal run toward Kribi's deep-water port and beaches connects two coastal poles by water.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Ideal for the sheltered estuary hops (Manoka, intra-district) and the Limbe coastal link inside 30nm, where calm channel water and short legs favour a fast, quiet, zero-wake craft that keeps a timetable pirogues cannot.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Reserved for the longer Douala-Kribi coastal express (~78nm) beyond Pioneer range, where range and open-coast running matter more than turn frequency.

signature_routes: Douala Bonanjo Waterfront ↔ Manoka Island — sheltered estuary-island hop
Douala ↔ Limbe — estuary-mouth crossing to the black-sand resort coast
Intra-estuary commuter hop — riverfront districts bypassing the Wouri bridge
Douala ↔ Kribi — southern coastal express to the deep-water port and beaches
transit_planning: Cameroon's transport investment has centred on the port, the second Wouri bridge and road corridors; passenger water transport on the estuary and coast remains informal, leaving room for a scheduled, app-bookable tier.

journeys.with_navier: A scheduled ~20 min estuary hop on a quiet foiling craft

journeys.today: A long congested drive around the estuary
journeys.with_navier: A direct ~40 min coastal crossing to Limbe's beaches
A short water hop bypassing the Wouri bridge

competitive_landscape: Estuary and coastal passenger movement is served by informal pirogues with no fixed schedule or weather resilience, and by an over-loaded road/bridge network; there is no clean, scheduled water operator, leaving open for a foiling tier with no incumbent on both the sheltered estuary and the resort coast.
seasonality: The Bight of Biafra has a long wet season (roughly March-November) with heavy rainfall around Mount Cameroon; the sheltered Wouri estuary supports year-round operation, while the exposed Limbe/Kribi coastal legs are best day-windowed in the wetter months.
regulatory_note: Maritime and inland-waterway transport fall under Cameroon's Ministry of Transport and port authority (PAD); passenger-vessel licensing and estuary navigation rules would frame any scheduled service.

precedents.what: Informal estuary pirogue transport at capacity
precedents.why_it_matters: Shows durable cross-water passenger demand a scheduled clean craft can serve reliably.
The user base already summons mobility by app, easing adoption of a booked water tier.
